touches.text: The only way to the database. WHY: the authentication is wrapped up in it, and every table has exactly one owner who gates every write; an ownerless table can't be made (Postgres refuses it).
Publishes a client tool (connect, read, write, query ...) that talks to the database over its socket, no bus hop: faster (2.3.7.1.1).

Who holds tables: every table of learning is a tree in the memory model (4.3.1.5), owned by the librarian and delegated to the devices that learn. A table that is not learning is an exception and names why; the bus's message table is the first (5.5.3.4.1).

Metrics land in one table so any metric can be reported fast from one place: at, name, source (the device/tool that recorded it), start, end, value, unit, subject (the thing measured), info (json). Fields not relevant to a source stay blank. Indexed on name and source by time. One thing (eg an inference call) may record several metrics in its short life, sharing one subject.
